title: Atomique: A Quantum Compiler for Reconfigurable Neutral Atom Arrays
problem: Fixed atom arrays require extensive SWAP operations for long-range qubit interactions, which is inefficient. The challenge is to strategically schedule coherent atom movements during circuit execution to reduce long-range interaction costs while respecting hardware constraints.
motivation: Reconfigurable neutral atom arrays offer improved scalability and fidelity, and strategic atom movement scheduling could significantly reduce compilation overhead and circuit depth.
method: Atomique compiles quantum circuits in three stages. First, it uses MAX k-Cut optimization on a gate frequency graph to assign logical qubits to physical atom arrays, minimizing the wasteful swap operations needed when qubits must interact across distances. Second, it fine-tunes the exact placement of each atom within an array to balance computational load and prevent exceeding hardware limits. Third, a router identifies quantum operations that can run simultaneously and schedules them together, reducing total execution time by strategically moving atoms between gates.
key_novelty: The core idea is to strategically move atoms during circuit execution—while maintaining their quantum coherence—to reduce long-range interaction overhead in reconfigurable neutral atom arrays.
contributions: Atomique compilation framework for reconfigurable neutral atom arrays
Qubit-array mapper using MAX k-Cut for SWAP overhead minimization
Qubit-atom mapper with load balancing and hardware constraint handling
Gate routing and parallel scheduling for circuit depth reduction
